history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V19 scored workload, mode, job count, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability ruling, acceptance decision, attribution metric, external-suite boundary, exact-parent contract, and publication boundary. It adds a separate zig-js-only no-JIT required-bytecode profile and repins the comparison runner because that explicit mode is part of the runner contract. The four arithmetic workloads are non-scored benchmark-first witnesses and do not enter cross-engine or aggregate results. Any later workload, option, checksum, mode, runner, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Adds explicit single_no_jit and attribution_no_jit modes with four arithmetic quickening witnesses while leaving every V19 scored row unchanged.

context_lifecycle_integration.publication_boundary: This remains the V19 zig-js-only cold lifecycle profile. V20 changes only the runner hash to include explicit no-JIT modes; no lifecycle option, scenario, checksum, telemetry, or evidence ruling changes.

no_jit_integration.timed_boundary: One invocation in one persistent production Context after ten reduced-work warmups; source/configuration, warmup, Context creation/destruction, attribution, and hardware snapshots are outside elapsed_ns.
no_jit_integration.publication_boundary: These rows freeze logical work and prove required-bytecode/no-native execution. Battery diagnostics and structural attribution are not performance evidence. A speed claim requires exact-parent, order-balanced, quiet-reference AC samples with stable required counters and unchanged controls.
